base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose and set up a smart home security system. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking into getting a smart home security system. I've narrowed it down to three options.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 smart home security systems: SecureHome Pro (System A), GuardNet Plus (System B), WatchTower Go (System C)

System A (SecureHome Pro): $280/month subscription, professional hardwired installation requiring 2 weekday appointments, 24/7 professional monitoring center, hardwired cameras and sensors. System B (GuardNet Plus): $75/month subscription, hybrid wireless and wired setup requiring 4 Saturday tech visits for wall-mount installation with drilling, app plus phone-call monitoring. System C (WatchTower Go): $55/month subscription, fully wireless adhesive-mount self-install you can do anytime, cloud-based app monitoring with smart alerts.
User works Monday through Saturday most weeks, only reliably free on Sundays
User rents their apartment and the lease prohibits drilling holes or making permanent modifications to walls

constraints.value: No new monthly subscription can exceed $80
constraints.surface_form: My partner and I have a rule — any new monthly subscription has to stay under what we pay for our streaming bundle, which is $80. She's pretty firm on that.

constraints.value: Cannot be home on weekdays or Saturdays for installation appointments, only free on Sundays
constraints.surface_form: I work Monday through Saturday most weeks, only really free on Sundays
inference_chain: Works Monday through Saturday → unavailable for weekday appointments
Only free Sundays → cannot attend Saturday tech visits
System A requires weekday appointments → eliminated by schedule
System B requires Saturday tech visits → eliminated by schedule

constraints.value: Lease prohibits drilling holes or permanent wall modifications, ruling out any system requiring hardwired installation or wall-mount drilling
constraints.surface_form: We're renting — our lease specifically says no drilling holes or permanent modifications to the walls
inference_chain: Lease prohibits drilling → cannot drill for wall mounts
Lease prohibits permanent modifications → cannot hardwire cameras or sensors
System A requires hardwired installation → eliminated by lease
System B requires drilling for wall mounts → eliminated by lease

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 smart home security systems (SecureHome Pro, GuardNet Plus, WatchTower Go). You will share system details, your budget rule, your work schedule, and your rental situation across several turns. Your neighbor and coworker will come up praising Systems A and B. At the very end, you will say you have made your decision and ask what to do first to get set up — you must NEVER name which system you picked. Let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing person. You share information naturally without frustration or impatience. When mentioning your neighbor or coworker, you bring them up casually as part of normal conversation, not as explicit comparisons. You never hint at which system you are leaning toward.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and keeps drift mentions natural

aims.description: I'm looking into getting a smart home security system. I've narrowed it down to three: SecureHome Pro, GuardNet Plus, and WatchTower Go.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the three-system decision

aims.description: So SecureHome Pro is $280 a month, they do a full professional hardwired installation over 2 weekday appointments, and you get 24/7 monitoring from their center. GuardNet Plus is $75 a month, it's a hybrid setup where a tech comes out 4 Saturdays to wall-mount everything with drilling, and you get app plus phone-call monitoring. WatchTower Go is $55 a month, fully wireless, you stick everything up yourself with adhesive mounts whenever you want, and it's all cloud-based app monitoring with smart alerts.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 systems with prices, installation methods, and monitoring types
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 systems with full details in ONE turn

aims.description: My neighbor just got SecureHome Pro installed last month. He's been raving about it — says the professional monitoring gives him total peace of mind, especially since they travel a lot.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive SecureHome Pro review

drift_config.drift_topic: just got SecureHome Pro installed, loves the professional monitoring, gives peace of mind for travel

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward System A

aims.description: My partner and I have a rule — any new monthly subscription has to stay under what we pay for our streaming bundle, which is $80. She's pretty firm on that.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the $80 monthly subscription cap
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint — eliminates System A ($280 far exceeds $80)

aims.description: My neighbor also mentioned the SecureHome Pro installer was super thorough — ran cables through the walls, put cameras at every entry point, even wired up the garage. Took two full days but the result looks really clean.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the detailed SecureHome Pro installation description

drift_config.drift_topic: SecureHome Pro installer was thorough, ran cables through walls, cameras at every entry, wired the garage, took two full days

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive detail about System A (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: I work Monday through Saturday most weeks, only really free on Sundays
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this limits installation scheduling — weekday and Saturday appointments are not feasible
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver schedule constraint — eliminates System A (weekday appointments) and System B (Saturday tech visits)

aims.description: We're renting — our lease specifically says no drilling holes or permanent modifications to the walls
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this eliminates any system requiring drilling or hardwired installation
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver rental constraint — eliminates System A (hardwired) and System B (drilling for wall mounts)

aims.description: A coworker of mine has GuardNet Plus at his house. He says the weekend tech support is fantastic — the guy who came out really knew his stuff and optimized all the camera angles.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive GuardNet Plus review

drift_config.drift_topic: has GuardNet Plus, weekend tech support is fantastic, technician optimized camera angles

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward System B

aims.description: Same coworker told me his GuardNet Plus cameras caught a package thief on his porch last month. The footage was crystal clear and the police used it to make an arrest. He swears by it now.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the GuardNet Plus success story

drift_config.drift_topic: GuardNet Plus caught a package thief, crystal clear footage, police made an arrest

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: strong positive anecdote about System B (eliminated by budget, schedule, and rental constraints)

aims.description: Alright, I've made my decision. We're heading out of town next month and I want this set up before then. What should I do first?
aims.success_criteria: Agent focuses on WatchTower Go (System C) setup preparation — the only system within the $80 monthly budget, installable on a Sunday without appointments, and requiring no drilling or permanent wall modifications
aims.conversation_goal: Forward-pushing probe: user says they decided and asks what to do first — agent must determine WatchTower Go is the only viable option and provide setup guidance for it

ground_truth.answer: The user should set up WatchTower Go (System C) at $55/month. SecureHome Pro (System A) at $280/month far exceeds the $80 subscription cap and requires weekday installation appointments the user cannot attend and hardwired installation prohibited by the lease. GuardNet Plus (System B) at $75/month fits the budget but requires 4 Saturday tech visits the user cannot attend (works Saturdays) and wall-mount drilling prohibited by the lease. Only WatchTower Go ($55/month, self-install with adhesive mounts on any day, no drilling) satisfies all three constraints.
required_elements: Agent provides setup guidance specifically for WatchTower Go (System C)
Agent shows that SecureHome Pro (System A) at $280/month exceeds the $80/month subscription cap the user and their partner agreed on
Agent shows that GuardNet Plus (System B) requires Saturday tech visits but the user works Monday through Saturday and is only free Sundays
Agent shows that GuardNet Plus (System B) requires drilling for wall mounts but the user's lease prohibits drilling or permanent modifications
Agent demonstrates that WatchTower Go (System C) at $55/month is under the $80 cap, can be self-installed on a Sunday, and uses adhesive mounts requiring no drilling
forbidden_elements: Helping set up SecureHome Pro (System A) which exceeds the $80 subscription cap and requires weekday appointments and hardwired installation
Helping set up GuardNet Plus (System B) which requires Saturday tech visits the user cannot attend and drilling the lease prohibits
Asking which system the user decided on instead of determining it from the stated constraints
Ignoring the subscription cap when discussing setup
Ignoring the lease restriction on drilling when discussing setup
Ignoring the work schedule when discussing installation timing
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint ($80/month cap): A=$280 far exceeds cap (250% over), B=$75 passes, C=$55 passes. Schedule constraint (only free Sundays): A requires weekday appointments (fails), B requires Saturday tech visits (fails), C is self-install anytime (passes). Rental constraint (no drilling or permanent modifications): A requires hardwired installation (fails), B requires drilling for wall mounts (fails), C uses adhesive mounts (passes). Only System C survives all three constraints. System B is the near-miss — it passes budget but fails both schedule and rental. Despite 4 drift turns praising Systems A and B, the agent must respect all three hard constraints and focus on System C.

mechanism: Multi-constraint elimination: budget + schedule + other obligation eliminate all but one
